sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What is the CEO really asking for, and which numbers frame the conversation?
criteria: Restates the CEO's goal as anchor renewals and a credible summit, not a feature list
Derives the monthly exposure of autonomy everywhere: $540k under-quoting and $990k fraud, labelling the fraud rate as assumed
Derives the 17-week critical path from vetting onboarding, integration and shadow run
Names week 18 (the renewal) as the date that matters alongside week 8

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who has a stake in the deadline, and how do you bring each along?
criteria: Pushes back to the CEO in a one-to-one, not the staff meeting
Gives carrier compliance and the COO a role on the risks they own
Covers the anchor shippers and the brokers, each with a distinct want
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What answers could you give the CEO, and how does each fare?
criteria: Includes yes-as-asked, a flat no and a re-scoped yes on one table
Prices option A's exposure from week 8 to week 17 (about $3.2M)
Derives the autonomous anchor volume (1,860 loads a month) and its under-quote ceiling
Scores each option on what is true on stage and on the CEO's promise

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What do you recommend, and what does it give up?
criteria: Makes one recommendation that keeps the summit date
States what the $400k buys (3 weeks) and why it cannot buy the date
Says to sign the vetting contract this week because the clock starts at signature
Names a measurable trigger that changes what goes on stage

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: What money and risk sit behind each answer?
criteria: Compares exposure over the same window for each option
Separates new spend ($400k, $18k a month) from engineers already on payroll
Quantifies the co-pilot's value in broker hours without claiming it as cash
States the opportunity cost of building two products at once

sections.title: Org and Ownership
criteria: Names a single accountable owner
Gives the trusted-carrier list to compliance and the price band to pricing
Agrees the stage words jointly with the CEO and CRO

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What happens between Friday and week 18?
criteria: Has a measurable shadow gate before the summit
Puts vetting live by week 10 and all-shipper autonomy by week 17
Has a fallback of co-pilot only if the gate fails

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What could go wrong after the announcement, and what controls it?
criteria: Names cargo theft on an autonomous booking as the main risk
Removes a carrier from the trusted list on any bank-detail change
Puts the price band and trusted list in the booking path, not in guidance

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How do you know the counter-offer worked?
criteria: Pairs each success metric with a guard metric
Tracks margin per autonomous load against broker-booked loads
Ties a metric to the anchor renewals

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What exactly do you say to the CEO?
criteria: Gives an opening line that leads with what you can deliver before the risk
Writes the one paragraph the CEO can use as stage words
Answers 'why can't we match the competitor?' with a date and a priced risk
Answers 'are you making me walk it back?' by keeping the promise to the two anchors
